title: Photosynthesis
summary: How plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
subject: Biology

sections.heading: What is Photosynthesis?
sections.body:
Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. It produces the oxygen we breathe and forms the base of most food chains.

The balanced equation:
6CO2 + 6H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6O2

sections.heading: Where Does It Happen?
sections.body: Photosynthesis takes place inside chloroplasts, mainly in leaves. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs blue and red light while reflecting green light - which is why leaves look green.

sections.heading: Two Stages
sections.body:
1. Light-dependent reactions (thylakoid membranes): light splits water, releasing oxygen and producing ATP and NADPH.

2. Calvin cycle (stroma): uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into glucose.
